q: For an ergodic measure-preserving system (X,μ,T) and a partition 𝒫 = {P₁,...,Pₖ}, the process {Xₙ = i : T^n x ∈ Pᵢ} is a stationary stochastic process. The KS entropy h_μ(T) equals the process entropy rate, and for Bernoulli systems the process is:
opts: A Markov chain of finite order
An i.i.d. process (the partition generates an independent sequence iff the system is Bernoulli w.r.t. 𝒫)
exp: A Bernoulli system is by definition measurably isomorphic to a Bernoulli shift. For the 'canonical' generating partition of a Bernoulli shift, the process {Xₙ} is i.i.d. (independent and identically distributed). The entropy is H(𝒫) = −Σ μ(Pᵢ)log μ(Pᵢ). Ornstein's theorem: the entropy determines the Bernoulli system up to isomorphism.
